ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Wilma Rudolph Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New headaches, word-finding pauses and right-hand clumsiness in a woman of 54: neurologic examination, MRI of the brain booked for the next morning, and neuro-oncology review booked. Concerns: Headaches on waking for three weeks, now most mornings; words that will not come for ten days; dropping things from the right hand; She wants the cause found quickly and explained plainly, without being talked around; She worries about falling and about losing her independence: her left leg was the weak one when she was a child, and now her right hand is clumsy. [S]

Two tablets every 6 hours as needed
Dexamethasone 4 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice a day with food, for symptomatic vasogenic edema, until surgery
One tablet twice a day with breakfast and lunch
Famotidine 20 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice a day while taking dexamethasone
Dexamethasone 2 mg oral tablet, one tablet twice a day after surgery, tapering
Dexamethasone 2 mg oral tablet: one tablet daily for one week, then half a tablet daily for one week, then stop
One tablet daily for a week, then half a tablet daily for a week

Once daily at bedtime, seven days a week, for 42 days
Sulfamethoxazole 800 mg and trimethoprim 160 mg oral tablet, one tablet three times a week (Monday, Wednesday and Friday) to prevent Pneumocystis pneumonia
One tablet on Monday, Wednesday and Friday

tr.td: MRI of the brain with and without contrast, with diffusion and perfusion: a 3.8 x 3.2 cm ring-enhancing mass in the left posterior frontal lobe, involving the posterior inferior frontal gyrus and abutting the precentral gyrus, with central necrosis, raised relative cerebral blood volume in the enhancing rim, no restricted diffusion in the necrotic center, surrounding FLAIR signal from edema, and 5 mm rightward midline shift; no other lesion
CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast to look for a primary cancer elsewhere: no mass, enlarged lymph node or other lesion

Functional MRI with diffusion tensor tractography for surgical planning: left-hemisphere language dominance; expressive language activation just in front of the mass; the corticospinal tract displaced but intact

Awake left frontal craniotomy with cortical and subcortical language and motor mapping and fluorescence-guided resection: gross total resection of the enhancing tumor, stopped at the mapped language sites. Pathology: glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 (necrosis and microvascular proliferation; IDH1 R132H immunostain negative and no IDH1 or IDH2 mutation on sequencing; ATRX retained; TERT promoter mutation; EGFR amplification; gain of chromosome 7 and loss of chromosome 10; CDKN2A homozygous deletion; histone H3 and BRAF wild-type). MGMT promoter methylated by pyrosequencing. Inpatient stay of three days, with mechanical and then low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis against venous thromboembolism from the day after surgery

MRI of the brain with and without contrast within 48 hours of surgery: no residual enhancing tumor; expected postoperative blood products; small area of restricted diffusion at the posterior margin from surgery; edema and midline shift less

Outpatient physical therapy assessment: mild weakness of the right hand and hip flexors after surgery; the left calf, weakened by polio in childhood, slightly smaller than the right with full strength; Timed Up and Go 9 seconds; home exercise program, home safety review and a fall plan
External beam radiotherapy to the resection cavity and margin, 60 Gy in 30 daily fractions over six weeks, with daily temozolomide; given in full on schedule

Outpatient palliative care consultation alongside cancer treatment: symptoms, coping, her understanding of the illness, goals and wishes, support for her family, and advance care planning; she named a health care agent (recorded in the confidential part of the chart) and completed an advance directive

MRI of the brain with and without contrast four weeks after chemoradiation: thin, smooth enhancement along the resection cavity with no nodular or new enhancement; FLAIR change around the cavity slightly less than after surgery; no new lesion. Treatment-related change; no progression (RANO 2.0); this scan is the new baseline
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, reviewing the advance directive completed with palliative care

Poliomyelitis in early childhood, leaving the left leg paralyzed or partly paralyzed, with the foot turned inward

Walking without the brace by about age 12; later an Olympic sprinter

tr.td: New headaches, word-finding pauses and right-hand clumsiness in a woman of 54: neurologic examination, MRI of the brain booked for the next morning, and neuro-oncology review booked
MRI result: left frontal mass with edema; dexamethasone, CT staging, neuro-oncology consultation with neurosurgery, and preparation for awake craniotomy
Review three weeks after awake craniotomy: pathology and molecular diagnosis, steroid taper, steroid-related hyperglycemia, falls, and the plan for radiotherapy with temozolomide
End of six weeks of radiotherapy with daily temozolomide: blood counts, liver tests, Pneumocystis prophylaxis, fatigue, mood, tumor-treating fields and an early palliative care referral
Post-chemoradiation MRI result, day 1 of adjuvant temozolomide, the start of tumor-treating fields, and the palliative care plan

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Urgent neuro-oncology consultation within one week, together with neurosurgery, to review the brain MRI with her and plan diagnosis and treatment if it shows a tumor

New progressive focal neurologic symptoms are imaged promptly: MRI of the brain with and without contrast within 24 hours, with same-day emergency care if she worsens, has a seizure, vomits or becomes drowsy; blood count, chemistry and A1c; no driving until the cause is known
Dexamethasone only for edema causing symptoms, at the lowest effective dose (4 mg twice a day), with famotidine and glucose checks, and tapered off as soon as possible after surgery

CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis to exclude another primary; functional MRI with tractography; awake craniotomy with language and motor mapping for maximal safe resection; MRI within 48 hours; integrated WHO CNS5 diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunostaining and IDH1 and IDH2 sequencing, ATRX, TERT promoter, EGFR, chromosome 7 and 10, CDKN2A, histone H3, BRAF and MGMT promoter methylation
No antiseizure prophylaxis, because she has had no seizure; seizure first aid taught to her and her household; levetiracetam if a seizure occurs

Venous thromboembolism: mechanical and then low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis in hospital after surgery; no routine prophylaxis at home; she is taught the signs of leg clot and pulmonary embolism and to report them the same day

Radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with temozolomide 75 mg/m2 daily, then six cycles of temozolomide 150 to 200 mg/m2 on days 1 to 5 of each 28-day cycle; Pneumocystis prophylaxis during concurrent treatment and while lymphopenia lasts; antiemetic before each dose; blood count weekly during chemoradiation and on day 22 of each adjuvant cycle; liver tests at baseline, mid-cycle 1 and before each cycle; MRI four weeks after radiotherapy and then every two to three months, read by RANO 2.0; clinical trial screening
GL-NCCN-CNS-2026, GL-EANO-GLIOMA-2021, GL-STUPP-2005, GL-HEGI-2005, GL-TMZ-LABEL, GL-ASCO-SNO-2022, GL-RANO-2023
Tumor-treating fields with adjuvant temozolomide, worn at least 18 hours a day, with scalp checks and skin care

Falls and mobility from the first visit: home safety review, fall plan, physical therapy assessment once the treatment plan is set, and a check at every visit of strength in both legs, since new right-sided weakness adds to a left leg weakened by polio in childhood; watch for new weakness, fatigue or pain that could signal post-polio syndrome
Early palliative care alongside cancer treatment: symptoms, coping, goals and advance care planning, and support for the people she chooses
Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain explanations with written information, and help to keep working as long as she wishes; she decides who receives information
MRI of the brain within 24 hours and a neuro-oncology and neurosurgery plan within one week of presentation
MRI the next morning; consultation three days after the first visit
Maximal safe resection within two weeks of the MRI, preserving language and right-hand strength
Gross total resection of the enhancing tumor nine days after the first visit; speech back to normal within days and right-hand strength nearly normal
Radiotherapy with daily temozolomide started within six weeks of surgery and completed on schedule
Started 26 days after surgery; 30 fractions and 42 days of temozolomide completed without a break
Dexamethasone tapered off within five weeks of surgery, with glucose back to normal
Off dexamethasone five weeks after surgery; glucose 96 mg/dL afterwards
No falls, and walking independently, through treatment
No falls; walks independently, with a cane only on uneven ground; home exercise program continued
Palliative care involved and her wishes recorded before adjuvant treatment begins
Palliative care consultation and advance directive completed eleven days before adjuvant cycle 1

list.item: Independent and working full time; walks without an aid; finds writing and buttons harder with the right hand for ten days. Examination: slight right pronator drift and right grip 4+/5, with full strength in both legs, a steady gait and no papilledema [S]
Alert and oriented; speech fluent with occasional pauses to find words and one or two substituted words; follows complex commands; repetition intact; PHQ-2 negative; no thoughts of self-harm [S]
